Commentary.Commentary: The players are back out on the field. Beth Mooney and skipper, Alyssa Healy come out to the middle. They don't really need it, but one eye could be on trying to finish this off quickly. should Australia, New Zealand and India finish with 6 points apiece. It will be the left-arm spin of Sadia Iqbal to Mooney first up.
... THE RUN CHASE ...
Well, Australia have never lost to Pakistan in any format in Women's games. They have certainly got themselves in pole position to maintain that record. Do stay tuned for the chase.

A really tough batting outing for Pakistan. They never really got off to a start, having a a boundaryless Powerplay, finishing with 23/2. No batter could adapt to the surface with only Aliya Riaz managing to get past 20. But she took too much time to get to even 20 and the pressure told on the other batters. The result was - not a single over went into double digits.

With Pakistan not attacking enough, Australia were spot on with their lines and lengths, not giving any letup. Everyone who bowled, kept the pressure on with Ash Gardner profiting the most, with 4 wickets, because those came at the back end of the innings. If truth be told, Australia could have restricted Pakistan to under 70 as well, because they missed a run out and as many as 3 catching opportunities. Still, they would be chasing at roughly around 4 runs an over.

It was not a great start for Australia though, as they lost Tayla Vlaeminck in the very first over, while trying to save a boundary. That meant Alyssa Healy was already a bowler short without even getting an over completed. But you look at that scorecard and see 6 bowlers utilized, without Ellyse Perry bowling a single ball. That tells you, if Vlaeminck had not been injured, Australia would have had 8 bowling options! Like in her previous two games, Megan Schutt was on the dot, setting the tone in the Powerplay but everyone bowled well. Or, was allowed to bowl well. Pakistan could just not get to terms with the pace of the deck and just crumbled under pressure.

Well, 82 is the lowest total made by any side in this World Cup so far. Majority felt that winning the toss and choosing to bowl was a bit of a questionable decision by Alyssa Healy but her bowlers have redefined every letter of the word discipline from the Oxford Dictionary. Absolutely supreme bowling display by the defending champions, that too, with a bowler short.

Commentary.Commentary: Now, we shall defintely have a DRINKS BREAK. Not needed to describe the exact state of Pakistan Women at the moment. At 40/5, they are in total tatters with everyone in the top 5 being dismissed. Cannot totally fault them as the bowling has been really good. Australia continue to tell users to practically see them bowl while trying to understand the meaning of the word discipline. The lines and lengths have been pretty consistent, with just the 2 wides so far. The fielding has been decent too, barring that one overthrow and one dropped catch. Pakistan simply are not able to find timing or power in their strokes and neither have they been able to read the pitch properly. But what's done cannot be undone. Can they recover now and get to 120? That could prove to be a fighting total. Here's Tahlia McGrath.

OUT! LBW! A bit of controversy regarding this decision but it will be a wicket for Australia. Pitched up right near the popping crease, around the pads. Sidra Amin goes for the flick but her bat gets jammed into the surface. The ball sneaks through and clatters into the front pad of Sidra. The Aussies appeal and the umpire straightway, raises the finger. Now, Amin goes for the review, indicating to her partner that she hit it. Here comes technology. The UltraEdge suggests no spike as the ball passes the bat while the Ball Tracker further confirms that the ball would have clipped the leg stump. Umpire's call it is on hitting and the decision stands. Amin is shocked as she continues telling her partner that she hit it. But cannot argue with technology, can we? Sidra Amin departs for 12 (18) and Pakistan Women are 23/3 after 6.2 overs. They retain their review but lose Amin.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Review justifed by Healy and MEGAN SCHUTT NOW BECOMES THE LEADING WICKET TAKER IN WOMEN'S T20IS! Beautiful bowling first up. Good seam position, keeping it upright and landing the ball on the seam, on a length, outside off. Sadaf Shamas looked to drive the ball on the front foot but the ball landed on the seam and bounced, taking the outside edge. Or it seemed because we did hear a noise. But the umpire did not hear and did not give it out. But the keeper, Alyssa Healy, who had taken it cleanly standing upto the stumps was 100 percent confident and sent it upstairs. Sure enough. UltraEdge detected a spike when the ball was close to the bat. The decision is reversed and the celebrations begin! Sadaf Shamas departs for 3 (6) and Pakistan Women are 18/2 after 5 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for the national anthems. Australia are the first team on paper for this game, so it will be Pakistan's anthem first, followed by Australia's. Right, 'Pak Sarzamin' and 'Advance Australia Fair' are done and we are ready for Game number 14 to begin! Some last-minute words by skipper Healy to her unit and off they go, spreading themselves onto the field. A different opening pair for Pakistan here as there is no Gull Feroza. The consistent batter, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, also the captain for this game, strides out confidently, with a new opening partner, Sidra Amin. We are informed that this is only the second time in Women's T20Is that both teams have captains who will be keeping wickets and also opening the batting! Of course, assuming that Alyssa will open later. It will be pace to kickstart things. Megan Schutt to start off, against the left-handed Muneeba. Here we go!

Before the game starts, let's look at how the results have come up in Dubai, especially in this World Cup. This is the 7th match at this venue and there has been a pattern brewing. In the first 4 games, the teams chasing won 3 times, but it has been 2 in 2 for the side batting first of late. Dew was expected but it has not arrived and batting under lights has been extremely difficult. Will it be the same tonight as well? Even LIsa Sthalekar, former Aussie World Cup champion, expressed her surprise with Healy looking to bowl. An experiment, maybe? Not sure, at this stage in a World Cup, even if you are on top.

Before the toss, Sophie Molineux had a chat with former West Indian great, Ian Bishop. Molineux says that she has spent a bit of time on the sidelines in the last few months but is eager to make up for that lost time now. On her couple of wickets in the previous game, Sophie says that everyone chipped in with wickets and there was a fresh bit of energy amongst the group. On playing their first game in Dubai, Molineux says that Australia will certainly have to adapt quickly to the conditions. Calls Pakistan a tough opposition but says that there has been some planning made in the dressing room and hopes that all of those get executed in this match.

PITCH REPORT - Alison Mitchell is at the pitchside and she starts with the weather being perfect for the game. She further informs that the ground dimensions are 63 metres and 57 metres on either side and the longest is 73 metres up straight. Carlos Brathwaite is alongside her to study the wicket and he says that the wicket looks to be a good one and will have a good consistent bounce throughout the game. There is going to be some turn on the surface and the fast bowlers will also get good bounce and swing with the new ball.

The stand-in skipper for Pakistan Women, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi says she is feeling good leading the pack and looking forward to winning this contest. Mentions that the news concerning Sana came as a setback for all but such things are not in one's hand and the entire squad feels sad for her. Informs that they have a couple of changes with Iram Javed replacing Fatima Sana and Sadaf Shamas replacing Gull Feroza. Closes by saying they need to put up a good total on board and make sure to bring out their A-game against a champion side.

Alyssa Healy, says that her reason to bowl first is more of a gut feel. Her first assessment is that the wicket is fresh and under lights, the ball might come onto the bat. But they also want to see how the conditions are and says that they will look to plan accordingly to come out and chase. Further adds that the wicket might grip and turn as the game progresses and they are prepared for that too. Informs that Tayla Vlaeminck comes in for Grace Harris. On being asked about that change, Healy stresses that it is more for impact for impact. In the previous game, they got Harris in, believing that the batting needed depth while for this one, they want to add an extra bowling option in the side.

Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Muneeba Ali Siddiqi (C) (WK), Sidra Amin, Nida Dar, Sadaf Shamas (IN FOR GULL FEROZA), Aliya Riaz, Iram Javed (IN FOR FATIMA SANA), Omaima Sohail, Tuba Hassan, Nashra Sundhu, Sadia Iqbal and Syeda Aroob Shah.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (C) (WK), Beth Mooney, Ellyse Perry, Ash Gardner, Phoebe Litchfield, Tahlia McGrath, Georgia Wareham, Annabel Sutherland, Sophie Molineux, Megan Schutt and Tayla Vlaeminck (IN FOR GRACE HARRIS).
TOSS - All ready for the flip of the coin. Tails is the call from Muneeba Ali Siddiqi, the stand-in skipper for Pakistan Women but it turns out as a Head. AUSTRALIA WOMEN ELECT TO CHASE.

It's nearly toss time. Live visual shows the two captains making their way to the middle with team sheets in hand. The stage is set for the crucial Group A match between Australia Women and Pakistan Women. Who will win the toss and choose to bat or bowl first? Stay tuned for the outcome of the toss.

Get ready for a thrilling encounter between the defending champions Australia Women and the challengers Pakistan Women. This T20 showdown promises non-stop action, drama, and thrill, amplified by a pitch that will test the skills of all the players. Will Australia's experience prevail or Pakistan's resilience spark an upset? The anticipation builds. Stay tuned for the toss and team updates in a bit.

The outcome of tonight's match carries substantial weight in the standings. If Pakistan Women win, a tight contest may ensue, with New Zealand, Pakistan and the loser of the Australia-India clash on Sunday, potentially tied at 4 points. An Australian victory, however, might lead to a three-way tie between Australia, New Zealand, and India at 6 points each, with Net Run Rate serving as the queenmaker for semifinal qualification. Of course, it is not just that. There need to be a few other permutations and combinations regarding the results of other matches to go some teams' way.

As Pakistan Women look to regain momentum after a tough last match against their arch rivals, they will be eager to capitalize on their opening win against Sri Lanka and fight for crucial points to keep their semifinal hopes alive. Every run and wicket will matter in this high-stakes clash.

On the other hand, Australia Women, captained by Alyssa Healy, are riding high after starting the tournament unbeaten, with two successive victories under their belt. Their last match saw them dominate New Zealand Women, showcasing their depth and skill, especially with impressive performances from Beth Mooney and the formidable bowling attack led by Megan Schutt.

Unfortunately, Pakistan's preparations have been impacted by the sad news of skipper Fatima Sana's father passing away. In her absence, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi will step up to lead the Women in Green as they look to bounce back after losing a closely fought contest to India in the last outing. .

Welcome everyone to this exhilarating showdown as the defending champions, Australia Women, take on Pakistan Women in a crucial Group A match at the Dubai International Stadium! This promises to be a thrilling encounter as both sides will be vying for a spot in the semifinals. A win today will grant the victorious side a significant advantage in the standings, adding immense pressure to this high-stakes encounter.

With each game, the competition in Group A is growing tougher and more intense. Now, as we approach match 14 at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium, Australia Women will face Pakistan Women in a crucial showdown. Both teams will be determined to seize these all-important two points as the race for advancement becomes increasingly fierce. Australia Women stand as the only undefeated team in Group A, with 4 points to their name, a clear reflection of their strength as defending champions. Pakistan Women, meanwhile, are coming off a defeat after a strong opening win, making it even more crucial for them to clinch victory here. However, getting past Australia will be anything but easy! The experience and depth of the Australian side has proven invaluable, as evidenced by their strong performances in challenging conditions across both games. With the top three batters shouldering the bulk of the run-scoring, the middle order has yet to face pressure, but their contribution will be key in providing that extra edge to set them apart. The bowling unit, led by Megan Schutt and Sophie Molineux, has been exceptional, though they might face a new challenge at this different venue. Australia may opt for an extra spin option, as they did in the previous match, but don’t be surprised if Darcie Brown returns to strengthen the pace attack. On the other hand, Pakistan Women enter this game after a tough loss against arch-rivals India and now face the daunting task of overcoming an in-form Australian side. However, they have the potential to turn the tide, especially with their strong bowling attack, which could be pivotal in shaping the outcome of this match. While their batting has been decent, it has largely relied on contributions from Nida Dar and skipper Fatima Sana Khan, who have worked hard to post competitive totals. For Pakistan to challenge Australia, the top order must step up, and the team will need to play out of their skin. Fatima Sana Khan has led the bowling unit brilliantly, but Sadia Iqbal could prove to be the most dangerous bowler to watch out for in this crucial encounter. With so much on the line, this clash promises to be a thrilling contest as both teams aim to strengthen their positions in a fiercely competitive points table.
